subject.title: [Architecture] Migration of transient plugin state to Agent-Scoped SQLite cache tables

question: Should external plugins receive a new generic agent-scoped TTL cache API, or should plugin authors compose the existing shared plugin-state and session-extension surfaces?
rationale: This choice defines a permanent public SDK and persisted-data ownership boundary, including identity, lifecycle, cleanup, backup, and migration semantics that cannot be safely inferred from the proposal alone.

options.title: Clarify existing surfaces
options.body: Document when plugins should use shared TTL plugin state versus session extensions, then add only narrow helpers proven necessary by a real plugin.

options.title: Design agent cache API
options.body: Approve a new public agent-scoped cache contract and specify identity, TTL, quotas, cleanup, backup, migration, and uninstall behavior before implementation.

options.title: Decline generic caching
options.body: Keep storage ownership explicit and require plugins to model durable state through existing plugin or session state APIs rather than a generic cache facade.

recommendation.title: Clarify existing surfaces
recommendation.body: Document when plugins should use shared TTL plugin state versus session extensions, then add only narrow helpers proven necessary by a real plugin.
